sentences.t: Petersburg amended its zoning code in 2024 to allow data centers by right in its M-1 light industrial and M-2 heavy industrial districts, which removed the public hearing for anything that fits those terms.
Four are now in the pipeline, and most of the city's own council members found out about them from a newspaper.
NuVu Real Estate, a Leesburg firm, has a three building campus on 75 acres at 2588 County Drive, between Interstate 95 and County Drive, which it puts at $1.1 billion and 300 megawatts.
It bought the land for $4.12 million in November 2025 and its site plan was approved in February 2026.
The company says the layout works inside the M-1 zoning with no variances or special exceptions requested and no impact on wetlands, and that it will use a closed loop water system.
As of late June 2026 the interim planning director, Jared Crews, said NuVu had not applied for a land disturbance permit.
The entry marks it under construction, carries the $1.1 billion and holds no capacity figure.
The projects surfaced through public documents in July 2026.
Ward 4 councilman Charlie Cuthbert said: "I had no clue about any of this until 12 noon today," and that on transparency, "it's like we're in a cave with the lights out."
Mayor Samuel Parham said he had learned of three of the four from the article itself, "I read about them in the news," and that "I'm in Ward 3, so none of them come to me to talk data centers."

Ward 1 councilman Marlow Jones, whose ward holds three of them, said: "This didn't have to go through us. It was already zoned and planned for, so some things slide under the cracks that we don't know until somebody posts it like this."

Ward 6 councilwoman Annette Smith-Lee said she knew nothing about the others: "If it was something that was just in the paper, we all should have got together to talk about it, instead of being blindsided here."
The city manager, John Altman, and the mayor did not answer the paper's request for comment.
Four data center sites are counted in Petersburg.
Menlo Equities' 104 megawatt campus shares these coordinates, the Wagner Properties site is three kilometres away and the Warrenton Group's five.
The 378 megawatt Hopewell Cogeneration plant is 12 kilometres off and the 386 megawatt Chesterfield plant 19.
Petersburg has written no moratorium and no zoning limit on data centers.

unconfirmed: No water withdrawal figure, construction schedule or tenant has been published, and our record holds no capacity although the developer's own figure is 300 megawatts. The Data Center Dynamics report our record cites refuses our requests. Whether a land disturbance permit has since been issued is unknown.

sentences.t: The record has a proposed data center at 1161 Wagner Road in Petersburg with no developer named.
The developer is Wagner Properties, led by Joseph Wagner, and the site plan for three buildings was approved in April 2026, nearly two years after it was first submitted.
The site is 73 acres, of which 27 would be developed.
The land is owned by GFYA LLC, tied to Jacob Manevich, a real estate agent from Potomac in Maryland, which bought it from Wagner Properties for $950,000 in 2024.
Legacy Engineering, of Fredericksburg, is working on it.
None of it went to a public hearing.
Petersburg amended its zoning code in 2024 to permit data centers by right in the M-1 and M-2 districts, which ended the hearing requirement.
As of late June 2026 neither Wagner nor NuVu had applied for a land disturbance permit.
The council found out with everybody else, in July 2026.
Ward 1 councilman Marlow Jones, who represents the ward holding three of the four projects, learned of them the day the story ran.

Ward 7 councilman Arnold Westbrook Jr., who had been involved with one of the other projects, said: "I'm not pro-data centers; I'm not against data centers. I'm (for) quality economic development in Petersburg."
Ward 4's Charlie Cuthbert criticised the zoning change that let data centers through without special use permits.
The entry holds no capacity figure and no acreage for this one.
Menlo Equities' 104 megawatt campus is three kilometres away, NuVu's three, the Warrenton Group's seven, and a Tract site the record marks suspended fifteen.
The 378 megawatt Hopewell Cogeneration plant is 11 kilometres off and the 51 megawatt Hopewell biomass station 12.
Wagner Road is under no moratorium, and the city has written no zoning limit on data centers either.

unconfirmed: No megawatt figure, square footage, tenant or construction date has been published for this campus and our record holds none. Why the site plan took nearly two years was not established. Wagner Properties was described here as being of Prince George, which the report does not say, so the home town has come out. The Data Center Dynamics report our record cites refuses requests.

sentences.t: The Warrenton Group wants a data center on land the city of Petersburg owns.
The Warrenton Group, a Washington firm that mostly builds flats, has a six building campus planned on 175 acres at 2233 Halifax Road, the former CSX Collier Yard, which is now city property.
It is working through a division called TWG Data, with engineering by Timmons Group.
Zoning was approved in 2025 and enlarged in February 2026 to take in three more parcels for access and wetland mitigation.
No site plan had been submitted when the documents were reported in July 2026.
The record carries 174 acres and no capacity figure.
Of the four Petersburg projects, this is the one a councilman knew about.
Ward 7's Arnold Westbrook Jr. had been involved with it, and said his focus was quality economic development rather than being pro data centers.

His colleagues had not heard of the others: Mayor Samuel Parham said of three of them "I read about them in the news," and Ward 4's Charlie Cuthbert said "I had no clue about any of this until 12 noon today."
Petersburg's 2024 zoning change, which allowed data centers by right in the M-1 and M-2 districts, is what removed the hearings.
Four data center sites are counted in Petersburg and three of them lie within seven kilometres of this one.
A Tract campus twelve kilometres away is recorded as suspended, and a 20 megawatt Hopewell project sits at an early stage sixteen kilometres off.
The 378 megawatt Hopewell Cogeneration plant is 17 kilometres away and the 386 megawatt Chesterfield plant 22.
Halifax Road carries no moratorium and no zoning limit on data centers.

unconfirmed: No megawatt figure, square footage, investment or tenant has been published. The terms on which the city is transferring or leasing the former rail yard were not established, nor whether a site plan has since been filed. Our 174 acres and the reported 175 differ by one.

sentences.t: Convergent VA LLC, a McLean land development company, first took this data center to the Fauquier County planning commission in May 2019 and got a 4 to 0 recommendation.
Then it went quiet for nearly five years.
Its partner, Jeff Price, said the proposal had been a little premature, and that opposition to data centers driven by the Amazon plan at Warrenton had made the developers pause.

It came back in April 2024: 140 acres south of the junction of U.S. 29 and 15 with James Madison Street, just west of the Lees Glen housing subdivision, four buildings of sixty feet totalling about a million square feet, cut down from six, with twelve foot screening berms and underground power lines.
The record carries 139 acres and no capacity figure.
The Piedmont Environmental Council put the revived application at 1.07 million square feet in four buildings over 65 feet tall, accepted for review on August 20, 2024.

Convergent is one of four proposals that together would make southern Fauquier what the Prince William Times called a data center alley; the others are SAMX, Gigaland and the Remington Technology Park, approved in 2020 and never built.
The council's objection to the cluster is arithmetic rather than sentiment.

It says the generation already in the county, Marsh Run at 513 megawatts, Remington at 608 and a 20 megawatt Dominion solar plant, is maxed out, and that four proposed rezonings would double the county's expected data center load and take the power of more than 500,000 homes.
Dominion has asked for two new substation locations at Remington to serve complexes needing over 400 megawatts.
Within three kilometres of this parcel the record holds Gigaland at 136 megawatts, the 300 megawatt Remington Technology Park, SAMX and the Remington Innovation Campus.
The Remington and Marsh Run gas plants are three and four kilometres away.
Thirteen data center sites are counted in Fauquier County; Warrenton banned them on July 1, 2025 and the county wrote zoning limits on December 14, 2023.

unconfirmed: No megawatt figure or tenant has been published and our record holds none. The Prince William Times report behind most of this page returned 429 on this pass and could not be re-read, so its account of the 2019 recommendation, Jeff Price's remarks and the revived application stands as previously checked rather than re-verified. Local reporting that could not be opened, in the Fauquier Times and Rappahannock News, indicates Convergent VA LLC pulled this application in late August 2026, one of three Remington-area withdrawals in a month; our record still marks it proposed and the withdrawal could not be confirmed from a page that would open.

sentences.t: Gigaland bought 202 acres near Remington, in Fauquier County, for $4 million in October 2023 and asked to rezone it from residential to business park for six data centers totalling 2.2 million square feet, a campus Baxtel puts at 800 megawatts.
The record carries 136 megawatts and the address 12270 Lucky Hill Road.
On June 18, 2025 the Fauquier County planning commission voted 4 to 1 to recommend refusing it.

The Piedmont Environmental Council, which described seven buildings and 2.2 million square feet on Lucky Hill Road, set out what was wrong with it: the applicant promised water quality improvements although the county water system already meets state and federal standards; the project would be one of four in the Lee District; the company actually behind Gigaland had never been publicly identified, and would neither name itself nor provide proof; and the proposal included four substations, more than appeared necessary, which raised the question of where new transmission lines would run across private land.
After losing the vote the developers added a $15 million proffer to the county's Purchase of Development Rights programme for farmland conservation.
The board of supervisors was due to decide on September 11, 2025, and the commission's recommendation did not bind it.
It did not get that far.

Gigaland dropped the plan after local opposition, the site being close to The Meadows residential neighbourhood, and set about a scaled down version: 847,400 square feet, two substations instead of four, and single storey buildings, planned for 2029.
One thing in the record deserves spelling out, because it is the part that runs when the grid cannot.

The Global Energy Monitor wiki records a backup power station owned outright by Remington Technology Park LP, listed also as the Gigaland data center power station, at 503.1 megawatts, running on diesel through Caterpillar internal combustion engines in three models, in pre-construction with a planned start in 2026.
That is most of the output of the 604 megawatt Remington gas plant, which is a kilometre from this site.
The project is marked proposed, with organised opposition recorded against it.
The Remington Technology Park at 300 megawatts and SAMX are both a kilometre away, Convergent two and the Remington Innovation Campus three.
Of the thirteen data center sites counted in Fauquier County, none is in Warrenton, which banned them outright on July 1, 2025.

unconfirmed: The company behind Gigaland has not been publicly identified. Reporting that could not be opened indicates the application was withdrawn in August 2025 and again on 17 August 2026, and that a co-founder named Art Lickunas wrote the second letter; none of that is carried above. Our 136 megawatts matches no figure in any source read: Baxtel puts the original campus at 800 megawatts and gives no figure for the scaled down version. The Piedmont Environmental Council counts seven buildings where Baxtel counts six, and that is unreconciled.

sentences.t: The Remington Innovation Campus is a proposed data center on 204 acres at 11462 Remington Road, in Fauquier County.
The record names no developer, holds no capacity figure, and gives two sources, a link into the county's permit self-service portal and a property records viewer, neither of which would open.
What is documented is the company it keeps.
Four proposals sit within three kilometres: SAMX at two, and Convergent Technology Park, Gigaland and the 300 megawatt Remington Technology Park at three.

The Piedmont Environmental Council counts Convergent at 1.07 million square feet in four buildings over 65 feet tall, Gigaland at 2.8 million square feet in ten buildings on about 200 acres, and SAMX at a million square feet on 55 acres with its own substation, alongside the Remington Technology Park at 1,286,000 square feet, approved but unbuilt.

It says four proposed rezonings would double the county's expected data center load and need the power of more than 500,000 homes, against generation it describes as already maxed out: Marsh Run at 513 megawatts, Remington at 608 and a 20 megawatt Dominion solar plant.
Water is the other half of the objection.
The council notes that 175 homes in Remington already sit in a FEMA flood zone along Tinpot Run, and that more hard surface from data centers threatens the town's revitalisation.
Its recommendation to the county is to build out only what is already permitted by right and approved, and to approve nothing further while the state works on its rules.
Thirteen data center sites are counted in Fauquier County.
The Remington gas plant is two kilometres from this parcel and Marsh Run four.
Warrenton banned data centers on July 1, 2025, Fauquier County wrote zoning limits on December 14, 2023, Culpeper County on September 2, 2025 and Prince William County on March 4, 2026.

unconfirmed: No applicant, building plan, square footage, power figure or hearing date was found in any page we could read. Reporting in the Fauquier Times and Rappahannock News, both of which refuse our requests, indicates the application was pulled hours before the planning commission was due to hear it, that it covered 11 parcels and sought to rezone about 182 acres from residential to business park, and that some of the land belonged to Lee District Supervisor Daron Culbertson and to his sister and mother, prompting calls for his recusal. None of that is carried above because we could not open the articles.

sentences.t: The Remington Technology Park, a data center approved in Fauquier County years ago, still has not been built.
The Piedmont Environmental Council lists the Remington Technology Park among Fauquier County's approved but unbuilt projects, at 1,286,000 square feet.
The Prince William Times, writing in 2024, recorded it as approved in 2020 and not yet constructed.
The entry puts it at 6980 Helm Drive on 234 acres at 300 megawatts, under the name Remington Technology Park Ltd Partnership, and marks it proposed rather than approved.
The partnership's name turns up attached to something else.

The Global Energy Monitor wiki records a 503.1 megawatt backup power station owned entirely by Remington Technology Park LP, listed also as the Gigaland data center power station, running on diesel through Caterpillar internal combustion engines in three models, in pre-construction with a planned start in 2026.
A standby plant of that size, for one campus, is most of the output of the 604 megawatt Remington gas plant two kilometres away.
Gigaland and SAMX are each a kilometre from here, Convergent two and the Remington Innovation Campus three.

The Piedmont Environmental Council says four proposed rezonings in this one village would double the county's expected data center load and take the power of more than 500,000 homes, and that Dominion has asked for two new substation locations at Remington for complexes needing over 400 megawatts.
Thirteen data center sites are counted in Fauquier County, and the rules have tightened around this one without touching it.
Warrenton banned data centers on July 1, 2025, the county wrote zoning limits on December 14, 2023, and Culpeper County followed on September 2, 2025.

unconfirmed: The date and terms of the 2020 approval, the building count and the tenant were not established in a page we could read. Our record's status of proposed conflicts with two accounts describing the project as approved. Whether the 503.1 megawatt diesel plant is for this campus, for Gigaland, or for both is not clear from the record that describes it.

sentences.t: SAMX is the smallest of the four data centers proposed at Remington, in Fauquier County, and it is not small.

The Piedmont Environmental Council describes it as a million square feet on 55 acres, in two buildings of about 45 feet with an on-site substation, with the applicant responding to county comments and having filed for a deadline extension.
The entry puts it at 11825 Remington Road, 55 acres, proposed, developer SAMX Data, with no capacity figure.
It sits in the middle of the cluster.

Gigaland and the Remington Technology Park are each a kilometre away, Convergent and the Remington Innovation Campus two, and an AWS campus at Stevensburg in Culpeper County is under construction fifteen kilometres off.
The part of this that reaches well beyond Remington is the wires.
Dominion Energy postponed its Morrisville line upgrade in April 2024, citing right of way limitations and the need to evaluate electrical and construction alternatives.
It has since asked for two new substation locations at Remington, which appear to be on the Gigaland property, to serve complexes needing over 400 megawatts.
A federal National Interest Electric Transmission Corridor designation, which would bypass state regulatory review, includes one short segment through northern Fauquier near Fiery Run.
The Remington gas plant is a kilometre from this parcel and Marsh Run two.
Thirteen data center sites are counted in Fauquier County, and Warrenton has banned them outright since July 1, 2025.

unconfirmed: No megawatt figure, tenant or hearing date has been published and our record holds none. Reports elsewhere that SAMX Data LLC applied in October 2023 to rezone 55.26 acres from agriculture to business park, that the buildings would be three storeys of 300,000 to 350,000 square feet, and that the land is owned by Superfood Farms LLC, come from pages we could not open and are not carried above.

sentences.t: CoreSite is adding to the data centers it already runs on Sunrise Valley Drive in Reston, in Fairfax County, and the people living beside them found out late.

Phase 2 of its V3 expansion, at 12367 Sunrise Valley Drive, would replace a vacant single storey building 19 feet tall with a data center of about 215,000 square feet standing 75 feet, on the 21.7 acre V3 campus next door at 12369.
The site plan went in on June 20, 2025, and county staff could approve it thirty days after the postmark.
It is one of four three storey buildings that would come to 943,600 square feet, two of them already up, taking CoreSite to 1.3 million square feet across its Reston sites.
The entry puts the site at 12379 A Sunrise Valley Drive on 13 acres, operating and expanding, with no capacity figure.
CoreSite's Mid-Atlantic general manager, Chris Lettiere, said the work would create an estimated 300 construction jobs and 50 new permanent ones.
Residents of the Cocquina Cluster objected.
Caitlin O'Dwyer called the existing facility "an absolute blight" and said the company had "made zero effort" at beautification.
The concerns were noise, traffic, light, the electrical grid and the effects of the evaporative cooling system on the weather.
The county's new rules do not help them.
Fairfax County's board of supervisors adopted a data center zoning amendment on September 10, 2024, effective the next day.
It does not reach applications approved before it, and CoreSite's development plan for this campus was approved in 2018.
Sixteen data center sites are counted in Fairfax County.
SAIC's building is two kilometres away, Digital Realty's VA3 four, AWS's Renaissance Technology Park under construction five, and NTT's Ashburn campus and CyrusOne's Sterling site six.
The nearest generation of any size is the 766 megawatt Potomac Energy Center, 19 kilometres off.
Montgomery County across the river wrote zoning limits on January 12, 2026 and a moratorium on June 12, and Prince George's County a moratorium on July 7.

unconfirmed: No megawatt figure is published for the campus and our record holds none. Our record names the entry for 12100 and 12098 Sunrise Valley Drive but gives the address as 12379 A and the area as 13 acres; the reporting puts VA1 and VA2 at 12100, on the former AOL site opened in 2008, and the V3 campus at 12369 on 21.7 acres, with the Phase 2 building at 12367, so which parcel our entry means is still unresolved. Water use by the evaporative cooling system, which is what residents asked about, is not published.

sentences.t: Science Applications International Corp is recorded as an operating data center on six acres at 12010 Sunset Hills Road in Reston, in Fairfax County.
The record names the entry after the tenant and files it under the landlord's company, Discovery Square LLC, with a Fairfax County property assessment page as its only source.
Two kilometres away is one that is unmistakably a data center, and it shows what the argument in Reston is actually about.

CoreSite's Phase 2 expansion, a 215,000 square foot building 75 feet tall at 12367 Sunrise Valley Drive, went in for site plan approval on June 20, 2025, one of four buildings that would total 943,600 square feet on the 21.7 acre V3 campus.
Residents of the Cocquina Cluster objected on noise, traffic, light and evaporative cooling, and Caitlin O'Dwyer called the existing facility "an absolute blight."
Fairfax County's 2024 data center rules do not apply to it, because its development plan was approved in 2018.
Those rules were adopted on September 10, 2024 and took effect the next day, revising where data centers are permitted in the county and to what standard.
Sixteen data center sites are recorded in Fairfax County, six of them within seven kilometres of this address.
The nearest generation of any size is the 766 megawatt Potomac Energy Center, 21 kilometres away.

Beyond the county line the rules are harder: Montgomery County wrote zoning limits on January 12, 2026 and a moratorium on June 12, Prince George's County a moratorium on July 7, Prince William County limits on March 4, 2026, and Warrenton a ban from July 1, 2025.

unconfirmed: Nothing describing a data center at 12010 Sunset Hills Road was found: no operator of the facility itself, no floor area, no power draw and no age. Searches on the address, on the company and on Fairfax County's Reston data center records turned up a corporate headquarters and no independent description of a data center there. Discovery Square is a pair of nine storey office buildings at 12010 and 12012 Sunset Hills Road completed in 2001, according to listings not treated as sources. Our record's six acres is the parcel, not a data hall.
